H4NY15154.name: Gonzalo Duran
H4NY15154.bio: Marine Corps veteran, founder and CEO of Devil Dog USA Inc., District Leader for the 79th Assembly District and Vice Chairman of the Bronx Conservative Party.

positions.stance: Proposes coordinating local and national organizations to fill gaps in veteran services, with legal support for veterans wrongly denied housing.
Supports more farmers markets and Health Bucks vouchers, limits on fast food in disadvantaged areas, and nutrition education in schools.
Supports more NYPD officers and surveillance in high-crime areas, bringing back cops who "walk the beat," and youth programs linking police and community.
Supports stronger regulations on developers, priority for current residents in affordable housing, and stronger protections against drastic rent increases.
Calls for stronger oversight of school funds, reasonable class sizes, and "a decreased emphasis on standardized testing."

H6NY15167.name: Andre Easton
H6NY15167.bio: Bronx public school English and special education teacher and organizer with the Party for Socialism and Liberation.

positions.stance: Supports repealing the Faircloth Amendment to build public housing, and federal rental assistance so no household pays more than 20% of income on rent.
Will fight to raise the federal minimum wage to $30 an hour.
Supports funding violence interruption programs, free mental health and drug treatment, and ending the 1033 Program that gives military gear to police.
Supports federally funded universal childcare through pre-K, equal school resources, cancelling all student debt and tuition-free higher education.
Supports "healthcare for everyone through a single-payer system, not tied to employment."

H4NY15147.name: Jose Vega
H4NY15147.bio: Political organizer and associate of the LaRouche Movement who ran as an independent in NY-15 in 2024.

positions.stance: Supports universal single-payer insurance, returning to the Hill-Burton Act standard, more doctors and nurses, and building or reopening hospitals.
Proposes a "Space CCC" youth program to rebuild the Bronx and the U.S. through nuclear power, high-speed rail, and new hospitals and schools.
Opposes current ICE deportations and proposes new residency agreements and two-to-four-year temporary work visas, such as for Mexican immigrants.
Says post-9/11 wars "must be put to an end" and calls for a foreign policy of peace through development.

H6PA03369.name: Dennis Mahoney
H6PA03369.bio: Humanitarian aid worker with a career in disaster relief and long-term development who builds cross-sector coalitions in Philadelphia.

positions.stance: Will fight to phase out benefits gradually instead of abruptly so "no family should become poorer because they started earning more."
Supports expanding affordable housing, first-time homeownership, housing near transit and job centers, and anti-displacement strategies.
Supports expanded transit, broadband affordability, workforce training and apprenticeships, and neighborhood opportunity hubs.
Supports restoring and expanding the Child Tax Credit, protecting food assistance and school meals, and increasing childcare affordability.
Supports tangled title reform, home repair access, neighborhood small-business growth, and pathways to homeownership.

H6IL02371.name: Ashley Banks
H6IL02371.bio: Has worked for a school bus company, the Chicago Transit Authority, and in truck driving, warehouse work, and ride-sharing.

positions.stance: Advocates federal investment to modernize roads, bridges, rail crossings, flood mitigation, broadband, and public transit in the district.
Supports strong public schools, career and technical education, apprenticeships, workforce training, and expanded access to higher education.
Will fight to secure and protect federal grants for local governments, schools, nonprofits, public safety, infrastructure, and health care.
Supports helping small businesses access capital and reducing "unnecessary regulatory burdens" to create jobs and revitalize commercial corridors.
Supports law enforcement while advancing evidence-based prison reform, rehabilitation, mental health and substance use treatment, and reentry programs.

H6IL04195.name: Chris Getty
H6IL04195.bio: Mayor of the Village of Lyons, former Lyons Township Supervisor, and licensed insurance producer.

positions.stance: Supports increasing affordable housing supply, lowering health care costs, and opposing "policies/tariffs that unnecessarily increase the cost of groceries, energy" and essentials.
Opposes unnecessary tax increases, supports closing loopholes for large tax breaks, and says Washington should reduce wasteful spending first.
Supports a secure border, modernized legal immigration, permanent protection for Dreamers, and an earned legal status process for long-term undocumented immigrants.
Supports lowering prescription drug costs, expanding affordable coverage, protecting people with pre-existing conditions, and increasing price transparency.
Supports strengthening public schools, expanding career and technical education and apprenticeships, and evaluating school choice by whether it helps all students.

H6OH01229.name: Nathan Weise
H6OH01229.bio: Chair of the Libertarian Party of Hamilton County and former Communications Director for the Libertarian Party of Ohio.

positions.stance: Says reducing government spending and controlling debt will help lower inflation and "make everyday life more affordable."
Supports an Ellis Island-style system with simpler legal entry and a path to permanent residency, demilitarized enforcement, and to "Abolish ICE and replace it with nothing."
Says agencies should be required to obtain warrants before accessing private information, with surveillance subject to strict constitutional limits.
Supports ending qualified immunity so government officials are held to the same legal standards as everyone else.
Says "reproductive decisions belong to the individual, not the government."

wiki:tracey-tackett.name: Tracey Tackett
wiki:tracey-tackett.bio: Assistant Mayor of Springfield, Ohio, and owner of Sip & Dipity Paint Bar for 12 years.

positions.stance: Will join other independents to form an Independent Caucus that forces "BOTH parties to negotiate issue by issue."
Supports securing borders, focusing enforcement on criminals, reforming asylum, expanding work visas, and a pathway to citizenship for long-term law-abiding residents.
Supports "an All of the Above energy policy" and eliminating bottlenecks that hold up new energy development.
Aims to give "more resources, more support, and more freedom to local government," including funding for frontline workers, police, and firefighters.
Supports independent non-partisan redistricting, free photo IDs for voting, and disclosure-first campaign finance to remove dark money.

H6OH13273.name: Sandeep Dixit
H6OH13273.bio: Engineer and small business owner who began as a shop-floor process engineer and served as president of a national Indian-American community organization.

positions.stance: Supports teaching STEM and AI in every Ohio public school, $500 million per district for vocational and skilled trades training, and raising the minimum wage.
Supports a basic health care guarantee with low-cost clinics and access to essential treatments like insulin, plus binding published hospital and insurer prices.
Supports ending federal taxation of Social Security benefits and no property tax increases for people on fixed incomes.
Supports strict environmental rules for data centers and penalties for privacy violations, "including surveillance tools like Flock Safety cameras."

H4NC04149.name: Guy Meilleur
H4NC04149.bio: Consulting arborist and educator; former lecturer and curator at North Carolina State University and instructor at Duke University.

positions.stance: Supports school choice, saying "allowing choice in education opens paths to academic success."
Supports freeing providers to offer more choice and reducing bureaucratic regulation to increase quality and access and decrease cost.
Opposes exclusionary and single-family zoning and supports allowing diverse housing types so cities can grow and remain affordable.
Says laws should be limited to violations of others' rights "through force or fraud" and punishment should be proportional to wrongdoing.
Says barring independent voters from serving on Boards of Elections "is unfair to them and bad for all of us."

H6NC05174.name: Robert Luffman
H6NC05174.bio: Truck driver with 25 years in the transportation industry.

positions.stance: Calls to "defend the environment," citing a UN report that being vegan is the most effective individual action to save the environment.
Says "stop funding wars" and stop arming Israel and other foreign regimes, using U.S. leverage to create peace through diplomacy.
Supports limiting the proliferation of data centers, saying their growth must be balanced against harm to water, energy, and land.
Says government should "represent the voters not special interests" and that abusers in the Epstein files should be prosecuted.
Says human trafficking and exploitation must be combated wherever they occur so that guilty parties are brought to justice.
Says "wars and genocides must end today," from Gaza to the Congo, with those responsible held accountable.
Supports universal health care, universal childcare, and "a complete overhaul of our mental health system."
Supports expanding wind and solar power, electric vehicle infrastructure, and "an indefinite moratorium on all data centers" until the industry is regulated.
Supports a $25 minimum wage, mandatory maternity, vacation and holiday leave, and repealing "right to work" and at-will employment laws.

H4NC10146.name: Steve Feldman
H4NC10146.bio: Physician and medical scientist specializing in dermatology who works to improve health care delivery.

positions.stance: Says the government "must spend less and pay down the debt" and calls balancing the federal budget the number one priority.
Supports a simpler system, such as a flat tax and sales tax with a full rebate on all income up to the poverty level and no other taxes.
Says "our military should defend our borders, not tell others how to live," and opposes sanctions, support for dictators, and Israel's treatment of Palestinians.
Says both programs are going broke and that raising the eligibility age should be considered, particularly for healthy, working people.
Supports putting "the power of markets to work" in health care to lower costs and widen access.

H6MI01309.name: LaVeta Davenport
H6MI01309.bio: Community organizer, nonprofit leader, life doula, mediator, and educator who founded the nonprofit Levadeh.

positions.stance: Says "I 100% align with the Green Party of Michigan 2026 Platform."
Supports covering everyone, employed or not, with single-payer universal health care ("Improved Medicare for All") built on Medicare.
Supports a living wage, free public education through a bachelor's degree, forgiving all student loans, and Universal Basic Income.
Says no one should be denied rights based on race, religion, sex, sexual orientation or gender identity, and "women have the right to choose abortion."
Supports hand-countable paper ballots, election audits, voting holidays, restoring Voting Rights Act protections, and getting money out of politics.

H6MI01275.name: Zebulon Featherly
H6MI01275.bio: Former traveling wind turbine technician trained in wind energy at a trade school.

positions.stance: Will fight to expand research, push clean energy advancements, cut waste, and demand accountability across government.
Will work to make "universal healthcare and tuition-free higher education a reality."
Will block new taxes on working families, demand that extreme wealth "finally pays its due," and push to raise the minimum wage.
Supports "a clear, fair path to citizenship for everyone building a life in America."
Supports protecting land and investing in dependable roads, bridges, modern internet, and energy infrastructure.
Seeks to end abortion and says "no to late term abortion in Michigan," arguing that "to end abortion, we too must show the victims."

H6MI01283.name: Arnett Satterla
H6MI01283.bio: Working man, husband, father, and small business owner.

positions.stance: Says "government should serve the people, not rule over them" and that Washington spends, regulates, and reaches too much.
Says "property rights are one of the foundations of freedom" and government should not treat owners and builders "like the problem."
Says the Second Amendment is about "self-defense and the right of free people to protect themselves, their families, and their communities."
Says government should need "a real reason, real limits, and real accountability" before it gets into people's private lives.
Supports lower taxes, saying every dollar government takes is one families, small businesses, and workers cannot use.
